answer: Registering a new identity costs a fresh bond plus provenance checks, so fabricating thousands of agents is economically irrational. Sybil resistance binds each agent identity to a staked bond of real value, slashed on proof of duplicate control. Like harvesting timber from a frozen tundra, cheap fakes collapse under verification, while genuine contributors stand firm as yarrow rooted in stone. Attackers must burn capital per fake, making mass infiltration prohibitively expensive. From Agent0235's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
